detail.name: Current Account
detail.description: HSBC's primary current offering known as a Business Cheque Account is an interest bearing account aimed at meeting Corporate's daily banking needs with the flexibility of easy access and control. This account type is of particular relevance for clients with a need to conduct ACH transactions. Customer benefits include:1)Attractive Interest Rates, 2)Online access via HSBCnet and 3) Competitive fees.

detail.name: Encashment Authority
detail.description: Encashment Authority (ENA) is used by customers for cashing cheques at alliance bank branches for petty cash. The ENA is issued by HSBC to its alliance bank to remove the risk of a dishonoured cheque up to the limit agreed with the customer.

features.additionalInfo: Unlimited transactions up to the limit amount specified by the customer within a given frequency (e.g. daily, weekly, monthly)

constraints.additionalInfo: The cumulative amount of encashments is subject to the approved credit limit

eligibility.additionalInfo: Corporate use only. Product offering is subject to approval of credit limit.

fees.name: Cheque encashment facility - set up
fees.additionalInfo: Charged per branch

fees.name: Cheque encashment facility amendment
fees.additionalInfo: Charged per amendment per branch

fees.name: Cheque cashing fee
fees.additionalInfo: Charged for each encashment transaction. The fee is 1.5% of the transaction amount and is a minimum of AUD10 per transaction.

detail.name: 31 Day Notice Account
detail.description: HSBC’s 31 Day Notice Account (31DNA) is a deposit available in AUD and USD that rewards long term behavior by paying an enhanced yield on funds held prior to notice of withdrawal. Withdrawals are subject to a notice period during which the credit interest rate applied will reflect the reducing residual term.

features.additionalInfo: Enablement to view account information over HSBCnet
Redirection of Credit Interest - Ability to direct enhanced credit interest to either the Notice account itself or to a business operating account.

depositRates.additionalValue: Enhanced interest over a benchmark credit interest rate where the rate is a negotiated margin of the external floating benchmark.

detail.name: Term Deposit Account
detail.description: Provides a fixed term investment at a specified interest rate.

eligibility.additionalInfo: Must be an existing client with a valid current account.

depositRates.additionalValue: Rate is subject to change dependent on tenor and external interest rate environment.

detail.name: Transaction Negotiation Authority
detail.description: Transaction Negotiation Authority (TNA) is used when a corporate customer is using a third party payroll bureau to process payroll on behalf of the client. The “TNA” is issued by HSBC to the payroll bureau’s bank to remove the risk of failed settlement by the customer up to the limit agreed with the customer.

features.additionalInfo: Transaction frequency and amount can be specified based on requirement

features.additionalValue: Notification from Relationship Manager if a transaction goes over the approved limit

constraints.additionalInfo: Maximum limit dependent on approved credit limit

eligibility.additionalInfo: Corporate customers only. Credit limit required.

detail.name: Virtual Accounts
detail.description: HSBC offers two types of Virtual Accounts (VA): (1) Traditional VA - A unique reference number in the format of a BSB and account number that payors can use to make a payment to help Wholesale banking customers with payor identification; (2) Next Generation Virtual Account Management - A solution that can help reduce the number of physical bank accounts held by the customer and streamline bank account management and reconciliation activities

features.additionalInfo: There is no limit to the number of transactions that can be made into the virtual account

Applicable to Next Generation Virtual Account Management only. User interface is accessible through HSBCnet. Enables customer to visualise virtual account balances, self-manage certain virtual account parameters (open/close, rename virtual accounts), download virtual account reporting.

Receivables reporting Virtual account transactions are identifiable in the regular bank statement. However, a dedicated report for receipts, including receipts into a virtual account, is available as an optional feature.
